street_pattern: narrow winding streets with central processional way
description: Third Dynasty capital featuring the Great Ziggurat, royal tombs, and a sophisticated canal-based economy. The city was organized around the ziggurat complex with residential quarters radiating outward.

street_pattern: precise grid with main streets 9m wide
description: Remarkably planned city of the Indus Valley Civilization with standardized brick construction, advanced drainage, and the Great Bath. Streets were oriented cardinally with sophisticated underground sewage.
reconstruction_notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site, partially excavated

street_pattern: grid aligned 15.5 degrees east of north
description: Largest pre-Columbian city in the Americas organized along the Avenue of the Dead. Multi-family apartment compounds housed the population in a planned urban grid centered on monumental pyramids.
reconstruction_notes: Extensive archaeological work ongoing since 19th century

street_pattern: irregular streets converging on the Agora
fortification_type: Long Walls connecting city to port
description: Classical Athens featured the Acropolis hilltop sanctuary, the democratic Agora below, and residential quarters spreading organically around these centers. The Long Walls secured access to the port of Piraeus.
reconstruction_notes: Extensive excavation of the Agora by American School since 1931

street_pattern: main arteries (Via Sacra) with organic side streets
description: Imperial Rome at its peak housed over 1 million people with sophisticated infrastructure including massive aqueducts, public baths, the Colosseum, and the imperial Forum complex.
reconstruction_notes: Continuous excavation and study for centuries

description: Tang Dynasty capital was the largest planned city in the ancient world. A strict grid of walled wards controlled movement, with two great markets serving east and west halves of the city.
reconstruction_notes: Modern Xi'an overlays much of the site

street_pattern: concentric rectangular zones centered on temples
water_management: massive baray reservoirs and canal network
description: The Khmer capital was a vast hydraulic city centered on temple-mountains like Angkor Wat. An elaborate water management system of barays and canals supported intensive rice agriculture for a metropolitan area spanning over 1000 sq km.
reconstruction_notes: Lidar surveys since 2012 revealed full urban extent

street_pattern: causeways and canals on a grid
description: Island capital of the Aztec empire built on Lake Texcoco with a population over 200,000. Connected to the mainland by causeways with removable bridges, featuring the Templo Mayor at center and the great Tlatelolco market.
reconstruction_notes: Templo Mayor excavated beneath modern Mexico City

description: Capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe featuring the Great Enclosure with its massive dry-stone walls built without mortar. The Hill Complex served as the royal residence with the Valley Ruins housing the general population.
reconstruction_notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site, key evidence of precolonial African urbanism

description: Major intellectual and trade center of the Songhai Empire featuring three great mosques (Djinguereber, Sankore, Sidi Yahia), the renowned University of Sankore, and bustling trans-Saharan trade markets.
reconstruction_notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site, manuscripts preservation ongoing
